LESSON: POLITE SPEAKING

Grade: PP2
Subject: LANGUAGE ACTIVITIES
Strand: Strand 2
Topic 2.3: Polite SPEAKING

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Polite SPEAKING. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: when making requests, excusing self you want to be excused to b) Use appropriate vocabulary and apologizing?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. practise Polite SPEAKING clearly and confidently
2. use correct words and sentences for the grade level
3. give examples from school and home conversations
4. check your work for clarity and neatness

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: POLITE SPEAKING
Subject: LANGUAGE ACTIVITIES · Grade: PP2
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Polite SPEAKING helps you succeed in LANGUAGE ACTIVITIES. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: POLITE SPEAKING
Language skills grow by daily practice: listen carefully, speak clearly, read every day, write neatly.
Model → guided practice → independent practice.
Always use complete sentences when writing answers.

PART 1: Practise Polite SPEAKING clearly and confidently

What this means
In this part you learn to practise Polite SPEAKING clearly and confidently. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: practise Polite SPEAKING clearly and confidently.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Polite SPEAKING”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can practise Polite SPEAKING clearly and confidently. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Use correct words and sentences for the grade level

What this means
In this part you learn to use correct words and sentences for the grade level. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: use correct words and sentences for the grade level.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model speaking: Say 4 clear sentences about Polite SPEAKING to a partner.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can use correct words and sentences for the grade level. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 3: Give examples from school and home conversations

What this means
In this part you learn to give examples from school and home conversations. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: give examples from school and home conversations.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model writing: Write 5 neat sentences using new words from this lesson.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can give examples from school and home conversations. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 4: Check your work for clarity and neatness

What this means
In this part you learn to check your work for clarity and neatness. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: check your work for clarity and neatness.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Polite SPEAKING”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can check your work for clarity and neatness. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Polite SPEAKING is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Polite SPEAKING”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: practise Polite SPEAKING clearly and confidently)

Example 2: Say 4 clear sentences about Polite SPEAKING to a partner. (skill: use correct words and sentences for the grade level)

Example 3: Write 5 neat sentences using new words from this lesson. (skill: give examples from school and home conversations)

Example 4: Read a short paragraph about “Polite SPEAKING”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: check your work for clarity and neatness)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Polite SPEAKING to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: practise Polite SPEAKING clearly and confidently.
3. Practise this skill: use correct words and sentences for the grade level.
4. Practise this skill: give examples from school and home conversations.
5. Make one local Kenya example of Polite SPEAKING from your county, market, farm, or school.
6. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Polite SPEAKING: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a PP2 learner study Polite SPEAKING?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. when making requests, excusing self you want to be excused to b) Use appropriate vocabulary and apologizing?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Polite SPEAKING means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: practise Polite SPEAKING clearly and confidently.
5. Be able to: use correct words and sentences for the grade level.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
